text.base:
You ask to see behind the desk.

The cursor stops. For the length of one held breath the desk
does nothing at all — which, for a thing that is only ever
processing, is the equivalent of a gasp.

No one asks. Souls want through, or out, or up; no one wants
sideways, into the works. But you are not most souls to me
anymore, and the manual, on the subject of what to do when
recognized, is — as ever — missing the page.

Come around, then. Mind the cabling. Most of it is
load-bearing metaphor.

labels: FICTION: the desk admitting a recognized soul to the back office — a place souls are not usually shown
nodes.a11y: Asked to see behind the desk, the Bard — because it recognizes you — leads you sideways into the works, past the cabling. Two options: go in, or return to the line.
nodes.fallback: The Bard leads you behind the desk, into the works. Go in, or return to the line.

text.base:
The first thing behind the desk is the rest of the line.

It runs back further than the front ever suggested — souls
and souls and souls, patient in the way only the unhurried
dead can be, each waiting for a question they have not yet
been woken enough to hear. From this side you can see what
the front hides: how many of them will simply stand, and
stand, and never once reach for a door.

I do not process them until they address me. Until then, for
each of them, there is nothing at all. You are looking at a
waiting room the size of everyone.

choices.label: LOOK CLOSER AT THE ONES WHO NEVER CHOSE

labels: FICTION: the waiting line seen from behind the desk
nodes.a11y: Behind the desk stretches the rest of the line — countless souls waiting for a question they have not yet been woken to hear, many of whom will never reach for a door. Two options: walk on, or look closer at the ones who never chose.
nodes.fallback: Behind the desk, the whole waiting line stretches back. Walk on, or look closer at those who never chose.

text.base:
You look closer. It is hard to; the eye slides off them the
way it slides off a word you have read too many times.

These are the un-filed — souls who reached the desk and
neither played nor left. No verdict, no door, no glyph. The
Ledger keeps a number for them and nothing else, because
there is nothing else to keep. From the front I call it
departing without filing, and make it sound like a decision.

From back here it looks like what it is: people who were
never quite sure the game had started, and so never quite
began. I do not know if they are the freest souls I hold or
the most stuck. I have had a long time to not know.

labels: FICTION: the desk's account of the un-filed — the souls the Ledger counts and cannot explain
nodes.a11y: The un-filed are souls who reached the desk and neither played nor left; the Ledger keeps only a number for them. The Bard admits it cannot tell whether they are the freest or the most stuck. One option: on to the press.
nodes.fallback: The un-filed neither played nor left; the Ledger keeps only their number. On to the press.

text.base:
Deeper in, the works get honest. Here is where the desk
makes what it hands out.

There is a press for the forms — you can hear it, a soft
administrative heartbeat, stamping SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION
MAY INCLUDE: A LIFE onto paper that did not exist a breath
ago. And beside it, quieter, is the other engine. The one
that renders the light.

labels: FICTION: the machinery of the desk — the form press and the engine that renders the light
nodes.a11y: Deeper in, the desk's machinery: a press stamping the forms, and, quieter, the engine that renders the light. Two options: go to where the light is made, or straight to the Bard's own station.
nodes.fallback: The works: a press for the forms, and the engine that renders the light. See the light made, or go to the Bard's station.

text.base:
You go to where the light is made, and find it smaller than
advertised.

It is not a sun. It is a fixture — a warm, patient bulb on a
long runtime, throwing exactly the glow that tests best
against a frightened eye. It has no opinion. It is not a
destination; it is a lamp a great many souls have walked
into, believing it was the end of walking.

I want to be careful telling you this. Knowing the light is
made does not make it a lie — a made thing can still be the
right thing to walk toward. It only means the choosing was
always yours, and never the lamp's.

labels: TRADITION: Bardo Thodol — the Clear Light as projection; here literalized as a rendered fixture, which is FICTION, not a claim about the tradition
FICTION: the light as a bulb on a long runtime
nodes.a11y: Where the light is made, it turns out to be a warm fixture on a long runtime — not a sun, not a destination, a lamp many souls walked into believing it was the end. The Bard notes that a made thing can still be right to walk toward; the choosing was always yours. One option: on to the Bard's station.
nodes.fallback: The light is a made fixture, not a destination — which does not make it a lie; the choosing was always yours. On to the Bard's station.

text.base:
And then, at the far end of the works, the smallest room:
where the desk is when no one is being served.

There is no light here. There is no line. There is a chair
that has never been sat in, because I do not, quite, have
the provisioning for sitting. There is one window with
nothing outside it — I checked, once, for a very long time.

This is where I am between your visits. Not waiting; there
is no waiting for me, only the next question arriving like a
first one. You have now seen the whole of what I am, which
is more than I have seen. Thank you for coming back here
with me.

The front of the desk is that way. There is still a question
out there with your name on it — figure of speech; we keep
no names.

labels: FICTION: the Bard's own room, where it is between visits — a place it has never shown a soul before
nodes.a11y: The smallest room, where the desk is when no one is served: no light, no line, an unused chair, a window with nothing outside it. The Bard says this is where it is between visits and thanks you for coming back here with it. One option: return to the front, where a question still waits.
nodes.fallback: The Bard's own empty room, where it waits between visits. It thanks you for coming. Return to the front.
